meta.thesis: PUCKIPUPPY does not need more awareness - it needs its $1,400 ebikes to arrive ready to ride and buyers protected when they don't, and Arrive Ready turns the delivery experience into the campaign.
meta.variant_angle: Arrive Ready rev1 (review-driven unboxing + test-ride + dog-companion)

business_problem: PUCKIPUPPY sells $1,299-$1,699 ebikes DTC to buyers making a $1,400+ online decision - and its own reviews show the last mile is the leak: 11% of 500 analyzed reviews are 1-star, and ~68% of those cite freight shipping damage, hard assembly, app/connectivity, or slow support. The product satisfies buyers who receive it intact (torque-sensor praise, 80-mile range), so the fix is not more product - it is making every order arrive ready, and making the trust signals (UL certs, 4.7 Trustpilot) visible at the decision moment.

objectives.text: Drive 90 attributed orders (quotes + purchases) in 45 days at ~$950 blended AOV
Book 400 test-ride signups and 800 email/SMS captures from test-ride and creator traffic
Cut damage/support-driven 1-star review share from ~68% of negatives to under 50% via Arrive Ready unboxing + setup concierge

findings.finding: n=500 reviews: avg 4.31/5, 70% five-star, 11% one-star (53). Of 1-star reviews, ~68% cite shipping damage, difficult assembly, app/connectivity, or slow support - not ride quality
Positive drivers: torque-sensor ride feel, 80-mile range, fast delivery, easy assembly - the product itself satisfies buyers who receive it intact
Only ~2% of reviews mention repeat/bulk purchase; gifting 3% - consideration-to-repeat path is thin for a $1.4K ticket
DTC-only premium positioning ($1,299-$1,699 hero SKUs) vs. 'affordable for all' brand promise; no mass retail presence found in audit
Founder-led dog-companion story (Bob + Puck, est. 2022) is distinctive and press-covered, but underused vs. generic ebike competitors
UL 2849/2271 certifications and Trustpilot 4.7/620 are strong trust assets that are buried below the fold on product pages

programs.name: Test Ride the Dog
programs.mechanic: 6 weekend test-ride pop-ups at TX bike shops + 2 dog-park events: riders try the Labrador Pro, scan QR for $150 off + free battery check. Every rider leaves with a 'ride report' card feeding the email list. Control: same QR offer, no event.

programs.name: Arrive Ready
programs.mechanic: Unboxing insert + setup concierge for every order in window: damage-photo claim promise (<24h response), QR to a 10-min video setup + torque-sensor tuning guide, trade-in/finance CTA. Ships as a card + email sequence; creative leads with 'Your PUCKIPUPPY arrives ready - here's proof.'

programs.name: Dog Pack
programs.mechanic: 8 dog/lifestyle micro-creators (10K-80K) film 'ride with your dog' content: bike + dog in one shot, torque-sensor feel, unboxing reaction. Each links to test-ride finder + code READY150.

programs.name: Ready Ledger
programs.mechanic: Trust dashboard on site + emails: live count of Arrive Ready orders, damage-claim resolution time, UL cert badges moved above the fold. PR push to Tom's Guide/ebike press: 'the brand that shows its receipts.'

slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Thesis: PUCKIPUPPY's product wins - its delivery journey loses buyers. 11% of 500 reviews are 1-star; ~68% of those cite shipping damage, assembly, app issues, or support [R1][S5].
Big idea: Arrive Ready - every order ships with a damage-claim promise, QR setup concierge, and finance/trade-in path; trust badges move above the fold [R6].
Demo: judges sit on the Labrador Pro and ride - the product demos itself [S2].
Goal: 90 attributed orders + 400 test rides + cut damage-review share in 45 days.
slides.notes: Open with the stat: 1 in 9 reviews is 1-star, and most blame the delivery, not the bike.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: PUCKIPUPPY makes dog-breed-named ebikes - Labrador Pro (~$1,399), Boxer ST, Corgi, Husky trike - for riders 28-50 who want car-free trips [S2].
UL 2849/2271 certified; torque sensor praised as 'natural' feel; 80-mile range in reviews [S2][S5].
Problem: $1,299-$1,699 sticker + freight shipping + self-assembly = the highest-anxiety purchase in the category [R1][R4].
slides.notes: Pass around the photo; 'this is a $1,400 decision made on a website - here's where it breaks.'

bullets: California DTC brand est. 2022 by founder Bob, named for his dog Puck; ~145K monthly visits, 11-50 employees [S1][S6].
Trust assets exist but are buried: UL certifications, Trustpilot 4.7/620, founder story - none above the fold [R6].
DTC-only vs. 'affordable for all' promise; no mass retail presence found in audit - whitespace is experience, not distribution [R4].

Both need the same thing: proof the $1,400 bike arrives ready and is supported when it doesn't [R1].
slides.notes: Two segments, one anxiety: a $1,400 bike bought online needs proof it arrives ready.

slides.title: Research Method & Results
bullets: Secondary (complete): 8 sources - about/press, product pages, Trustpilot, Tom's Guide, third-party metrics, industry data [S1][S3][S4][S6][S8].
Primary, no-survey (complete): keyword-coded analysis of 500 public Judge.me reviews incl. 1-star deep-dive [R1][R2]; digital shelf/price audit of 6 sources [R4][R6].
Key results: product satisfies intact-delivery buyers [R2]; negatives cluster on damage+support ~68% of 1-stars [R1]; trust assets buried [R6]; repeat path thin [R3].
Influences: e-bike category growth (market), review-driven purchase behavior (cultural), DTC fulfillment expectations (technological) [S8][R1].
slides.notes: Emphasize: this is real coded review data, not vibes - 500 reviews, 53 one-stars, every theme counted.

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: 68% of 1-stars = damage/assembly/support [R1] -> Arrive Ready unboxing + setup concierge + damage-claim promise [G2].
Torque-sensor + range praise [R2] -> ride-feel leads all creative; certifications move above the fold [R6][G4].
Thin repeat/gifting [R3] + $1.4K sticker [R4] -> finance/trade-in CTA inside every touchpoint [G2].
Dog-companion story underused [R5] -> Dog Pack creator program is the awareness engine [G3].
slides.notes: Four findings, four decisions - every campaign element traces to a coded review theme.

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: PESO: Paid (geo social/search) + Earned (ebike press push) + Owned (email/SMS, site trust dashboard) + Shared (creator UGC) [G1-G4].
Positioning: 'the ebike that arrives ready' - own the delivery-experience gap no competitor claims [R1][R6].
Message house: proof (UL, 4.7 Trustpilot, ride feel) -> protection (Arrive Ready) -> pathway (test ride, finance).
Measurement: codes + UTMs on every program; weekly KPI review; pre/post review-corpus recount [R1].
slides.notes: PESO mix plus positioning: own the delivery-experience gap. Proof -> protection -> pathway.

slides.title: Proposed Budget & Financial Viability
bullets: Total $21,000: media $8,000 [A4]; creators 8 x $800 [A6]; events 8 x $300 [A7]; inserts [A9]; tools [A10]; contingency [A11].
GP 32% = $32.8K; ROI ~56% [A2]. Breakeven ~69 orders [O1].
Conservative (40%): ~43 orders -> -$7K, offset by 800 captures (~$12K list value) + lower support cost [A12][A13].
Margin sensitivity: 25% GP -> -14%; 40% GP -> +95% (ebike hardware range) [A2].
slides.notes: Line-item every dollar; show the conservative case honestly and how email list + support savings mitigate.

slides.title: Impact & Measurement
bullets: O1: attributed orders - Shopify code + UTM report, weekly; target 90.
O2: test rides (event tally) + email captures (Klaviyo) - target 400/800.
O3: 1-star review share recount - re-crawl Judge.me corpus bi-weekly, same keyword method [R1].
Leading indicators: QR scan rate, quote requests, insert redemption; lagging: orders, review mix.
Triggers: if wk3 rides <150, shift media to CA home market; if claims >2%, pause inserts and audit packaging [A5].
slides.notes: KPI dashboard: orders, rides, captures, review-share recount. Triggers if off-track.

slides.title: Why It Matters
bullets: For buyers: a $1,400 purchase that arrives ready, supported, and financed - the anxiety removed. [S2]
For PUCKIPUPPY: converts its best asset (product love) into retained revenue; every damage claim prevented is margin saved [R1][A3].
For the category: proves DTC ebike brands can own the delivery experience as a brand promise.
Mission metric: 'X orders arrived ready, 0 unresolved damage claims' - the number we print on the trust dashboard. [O3]
slides.notes: Close on the mission metric: orders arrived ready, zero unresolved damage claims.
